cands.bio: Mayor of High Point, North Carolina, since 2023 and a High Point City Council member from 2019. Founder of the consulting firm Change Often. Former music teacher. Democratic nominee for North Carolina's 6th Congressional District. Born in Utica, New York, and raised in High Point.

endorsements.text: In his Ballotpedia survey he lists support from former Rep. Kathy Manning, Nancy Pelosi (through PAC to the Future), former Education Secretary Arne Duncan, Guilford County Commission Chair Skip Alston and Guilford County Board of Education Chair Deena Hayes-Greene. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: We found no stated position from Jefferson on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, abortion, gun policy or school vouchers. We found no documented deeds from his time as mayor or council member on rezonings, development approvals, tax rates or police pay; the pages we had list campaign claims, not official records. His exact birth date and the year he moved to North Carolina are not given. His housing platform mentions modernizing zoning and protecting neighborhood character, but it does not clearly say whether he would slow or speed growth. His campaign claims about crime and housing results (for example, a 75% drop in homicides, a 67% drop in violent crime, and a $40M housing fund) could not be checked against independent sources.

workers-first.evidence: His campaign website says he will protect American wages with E-Verify and supports the bipartisan Border Act of 2024 to add border agents, judges and fentanyl detection at ports of entry. It also says he would expand legal visa pathways.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign website says that in Congress he would fund modern policing tools, body cameras and officer wellness programs, and expand mental-health crisis response teams. It does not mention officer pay or pensions.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign website says he will raise teacher pay and reduce class sizes. It does not state a position on vouchers, charters or school choice.

cands.bio: Republican U.S. representative for North Carolina's 6th District since January 2025. Graduated from UNC Charlotte with a political science degree. Worked as a constituent liaison for Ted Budd and as a lobbyist for Blue Cross Blue Shield of North Carolina. First elected in 2024.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by President Donald Trump for the 2026 race (listed on Ballotpedia and stated on his campaign site).
In 2024, endorsed by U.S. Sen. Ted Budd, Donald Trump and Veterans for America First.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from McDowell on data centers, development or growth, property taxes, limits on investor or foreign purchases of homes and land, teacher pay or school choice, or on police pay and pensions. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys in 2024 or 2026. We found no documented controversies and no foreign ties in the pages reviewed. His time of residence in North Carolina is not described beyond birth and upbringing, and no source gives exact years for his jobs. His work for Richard Hudson's campaign appears only on Wikipedia, which gives no dates.

votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.
